title: Ocarina of Time's Lost Expansion Became Master Quest
hook:
In 1997 Miyamoto said Ocarina of Time could get an expansion disk on the 64DD. The add-on flopped, and the remixed dungeons surfaced six years later as Master Quest. Would you play a Master Quest of the new remake?
Gameplay is from Shards of Irsa, a game I'm making.
script: Did you know Ocarina of Time was supposed to get an expansion disk that Nintendo never released? Back in 1997, Shigeru Miyamoto said a second quest version of the game could easily be released on the 64DD. He described it as something like Zelda 1.5, an expansion kit to keep players going longer. Fans came to know it as Ura Zelda. The 64DD was a disk drive that bolted onto the bottom of the Nintendo 64. It launched only in Japan in December 1999 and was shut down in February 2001. Ura Zelda went down with it. Eiji Aonuma later said his team had been told to repurpose Ocarina's dungeons and make a game out of them. That work did not vanish. In 2003, Nintendo put it on a GameCube bonus disc for Wind Waker pre-orders and called it Master Quest. It came back again in 2011, mirrored and with double damage, inside Ocarina of Time 3D on the 3DS. Now the brand new Switch 2 remake launched on November fifth. Nintendo says it sold over 5.2 million copies in four days, its fastest start yet on the system. Would you play a Master Quest of the new remake? Follow for more gaming history.
